input.summary: Idaho Code § 63-3024A sets the food tax credit (formerly the grocery credit) at $155 per person for tax year 2025 and each year after. The credit is refundable: any part above tax due is paid out as a refund. The household is one 56-year-old resident filer with no dependents. Nothing triggers proration: the head is not SNAP-eligible and no incarceration is listed. That gives $155. The engine awarded the full $155 base credit for all 12 months, which matches the law. The consensus answer of $0 rests on claims that the credit is nonrefundable, repealed or phased out, and all three are wrong. The 2026 bills that would have changed the credit (HB 605 and HB 633, which would have repealed it) were only printed and filed, so neither became law.

citations.source: Idaho Code § 63-3024A, Food tax credits and refunds (as amended by 2025 HB 231)
citations.quote: For tax year 2025 and each year thereafter, the credit is one hundred fifty-five dollars ($155).

citations.source: Idaho Code § 63-3024A, Food tax credits and refunds
citations.quote: If taxes due are less than the total credit allowed, the taxpayer shall be paid a refund equal to the balance of the unused credit.

citations.source: Idaho Code § 63-3024A, Food tax credits and refunds
citations.quote: the credit or refund allowed under this section shall be in proportion to the number of months of the year in which no assistance was received

citations.source: Idaho State Tax Commission, Idaho Food Tax Credit
citations.quote: For most Idaho residents it's $155 per person or up to $250 if you submit receipts for sales tax paid for food.
